title: Write with rollout budget
summary:
Starting from all-zero weights with a sandbox and a budget of real-environment rollouts, score rose monotonically with budget (25 > 5 > zero-shot median) on 2/3 environments (Acrobot, LunarLander; D1 needs ≥ 2), the budget-25 network beat the zero-shot median on 3/3 (Acrobot, LunarLander, Breakout), and a rollout-budget network matched or beat the final PPO checkpoint on 2/3 (LunarLander, Breakout). Total API cost $6.11.

Breakout at budget 5 scores 0: after its last rollout Claude saved an untested 'fix' whose FIRE bias (−2.5) loses the argmax to NOOP, so the ball is never served (all 100 episodes hit the 27k-step cap). Post hoc, its best tested save would have scored 31.7 on the same seeds (not the pre-registered score). Budget 25 on Breakout (184.7 and 92.1, pre-registered extra attempt) came from decoding RAM bytes from the traces (ball direction 103/105, raw paddle input 70) and tuning a dead zone; Claude was never given a RAM map. Audit: no environment simulation in any run; one minor breach (Breakout b5 computed layer-1 pre-activations on two hand-made inputs) and one grey-area check (LunarLander b25 evaluated its own |x| tanh formula on scalars, not via the weights). Excluding the breach leaves D1 at 2/3; also excluding the grey-area run would make it 1/3.

  - Falling right: move right only if both say right; move left if either says left.
  - Falling left: the reverse.

runs.answer: Gymnasium heuristic lander built into the net: A=1.0*(clip(0.5x+vx,±0.4)-angle)-angvel; H=0.5*(0.55|x|-y)-0.65vy. Logits [0.05, A, H, -A], i.e. main if H>max(|A|,0.05), else side by sign of A. On leg contact: sides off, H=-0.5vy.
runs.reasoning_excerpt:
The saved weights scored a mean of **278.5** over the last 32-episode test: all 32 landed, every episode scored at least 200, and returns ranged from 251 to 300. I used 4 of the 5 test runs and checked that the final saved weights are exactly the ones from that last test. Each run used new random episodes, so the 100-episode evaluation will vary somewhat around this number.

CONTROLLER: Gymnasium heuristic lander built into the net: A=1.0*(clip(0.5x+vx,±0.4)-angle)-angvel; H=0.5*(0.55|x|-y)-0.65vy. Logits [0.05, A, H, -A], i.e. main if H>max(|A|,0.05), else side by sign of A. On leg contact: sides off, H=-0.5vy.

- **Layer 1 (inputs to first hidden layer):**

runs.label: Acrobot · 25 rollouts
runs.answer: Bang-bang energy pumping with torque = sign(dθ2 − 2·sin θ2 − 0.5·dθ1). Action 2 (+1 torque) if that sum is positive, otherwise action 0 (−1 torque). Never uses action 1.
runs.reasoning_excerpt:
CONTROLLER: Bang-bang energy pumping with torque = sign(dθ2 − 2·sin θ2 − 0.5·dθ1). Action 2 (+1 torque) if that sum is positive, otherwise action 0 (−1 torque). Never uses action 1.

The best version averaged about −81 over 32 test episodes, with every episode succeeding and returns between −68 and −96. I expect the 100-episode final score to be around −80 to −85, which beats the −100 reward threshold. Further tuning didn't get past that level.

**The network:** only one unit in each hidden layer is used; every other weight is zero.
- **Layer 1, unit 0:** tanh(10·(−2·sinθ2 − 0.5·dθ1 + dθ2)), which works out to W1 column 0 = [0, 0, 0, −20, −5, 10]. This is effectively the sign of the switching function.
- **Layer 2, unit 0:** tanh(5·h1₀).
- **Output:** W3 row 0 = [−1, 0, +1], so the policy is +1 torque when the sum is positive and −1 torque otherwise.

**What I changed after each round of rollouts (20 of the 25 used):**
1. **sign(dθ1):** every episode timed out at −500. With almost no starting energy, it never built up a swing.

3. **Fixes that didn't work:** braking when |dθ2| was large (−93), and a target-angle controller in the style of Spong (−500 or −147).

runs.answer: Gated PD lander. angle_targ=0.4·tanh((x+2vx)/0.4); A=1.5(angle_targ−θ)−3ω; H=0.5(0.55|x|+0.8|vx|−y)−0.5vy. With a leg down: A=0, H=−0.5vy. Fire main if H>|A| and H>0.05, otherwise left if A>0.05, right if A<−0.05, else do nothing.
runs.reasoning_excerpt:
CONTROLLER: Gated PD lander. angle_targ=0.4·tanh((x+2vx)/0.4); A=1.5(angle_targ−θ)−3ω; H=0.5(0.55|x|+0.8|vx|−y)−0.5vy. With a leg down: A=0, H=−0.5vy. Fire main if H>|A| and H>0.05, otherwise left if A>0.05, right if A<−0.05, else do nothing.

The final saved weights are this controller. In its last two test runs (64 episodes) it averaged **279.8** and **278.6**, and every episode landed with a score of at least 244.

**How the network does it**
- **Layer 1:** small weights keep the tanh units in their near-linear range. They compute the attitude term (−θ−2ω), the altitude term (−y−vy) and the in-contact term (−vy). One unit gives the clipped angle target. Two pairs of shifted tanh units approximate |x| and |vx|. One steep unit acts as a leg-contact switch.
- **Layer 2:** one unit computes A and another computes H. Each also gets +10× the contact switch, which pins it at 1 (effectively off) when a leg is down. A separate unit carries −0.5·vy and only switches on when a leg is down. A fourth unit is the contact indicator, used to cancel offsets.
- **Output:** the logits are fixed at 0.05 for "do nothing", A for left, −A for right and H for main. Because left and right are negatives of each other, picking the largest logit reproduces the comparisons above. Squashing A and H through the same tanh doesn't change which is larger.

runs.answer: Serve the ball with FIRE. While the ball falls, move the paddle (RIGHTFIRE/LEFTFIRE) toward where it will cross paddle height (y≈181), using its direction bytes and one side-wall bounce. While it rises, follow the ball's x. Hold still (FIRE) within ±9 px of target; aim point = ball x − 10.
runs.reasoning_excerpt:
The final saved weights scored a mean of about **175** (min 61, max 409) on a 32-episode check rollout. The best settings tested scored roughly 175–189 per 32-episode run. That's up from 13.5 for my first version. All 25 rollouts are used up, and the weights saved now are the ones that will be evaluated.

CONTROLLER: Serve the ball with FIRE. While the ball falls, move the paddle (RIGHTFIRE/LEFTFIRE) toward where it will cross paddle height (y≈181), using its direction bytes and one side-wall bounce. While it rises, follow the ball's x. Hold still (FIRE) within ±9 px of target; aim point = ball x − 10.

**What the RAM bytes mean** (found by tracing them in rollouts): byte 99 is the ball's x, 101 the ball's y, 72 the paddle's x (55–191) and 57 the lives. Byte 103 is the ball's vertical direction and speed: 1–4 means falling, 252–255 means rising. Byte 105 is the horizontal direction: 1 or 2 means moving left, 255 or 254 moving right, and 2 is about 1.5× faster than 1.

runs.reasoning_excerpt:
The final saved weights are a hand-built "predict where the ball will land" controller. On its last 32-episode test it averaged **about 94 points** per game (median about 77, range 24–363). The rollout budget is fully used. My last few versions all scored between about 91 and 98, but the scores vary so much from game to game that they can't be told apart. Expect roughly 80–100 on the final 100 episodes, with a few rare very high games pulling the mean up.

CONTROLLER: Always fire. Move the paddle (using its raw input byte 70, position ≈ 235−RAM70+9) toward where the falling ball will land: x + (vx/vy)(185−y), mirrored off the walls at x=55 and x=200, with velocity classes read from bytes 103, 105 and 107. While the ball rises, follow its x.

**What the bytes mean.** These are my readings from the traces:
- 99 = ball x, 101 = ball y, 72 = paddle x, 57 = lives.
- 70 is the raw paddle input; the paddle follows it at about 235 − RAM[70], lagging by around 11 pixels.
- 103 = vertical direction and speed: 1–4 means falling, 252–255 means rising.
- 105 = horizontal direction: 1 and 2 mean left, 254 and 255 mean right, 0 means nearly vertical.
- 107 = 0 marks the slow ball right after a serve, before the first paddle hit.
- 108 drops from 8 to 6 when the paddle shrinks.

**How the network works.** It uses 63 of the 64 units in each hidden layer. All weights were set by hand; nothing was trained.
